extracted.intended_audience: federal agency procurement officials, ADP managers, agency heads and senior staff responsible for implementing OMB Circular A-76 for ADP
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for executive agencies on whether to provide automatic data processing (ADP) services in-house or rely on competitive commercial sources under OMB Circular A-76, including planning, acquisition, cost-comparison, exceptions, and termination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy preference for commercial ADP services
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with the Government's general policy of reliance on the private sector, agencies will obtain ADP services from competitive commercial sources in preference to direct operation of in-house activities, except as provided in paragraph 5 of Circular No. A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The service approach shifts the agency role from performance to management: agencies must retain in-house expertise sufficient to prepare service performance specifications and monitor contractor performance. New starts, expansions, upgrades or modernizations require review under A-76. (Draft Transmittal Memorandum ¶4; Circular ¶2–4)

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and scope of A-76 application to ADP
rubrics_metrics.description: The transmittal memorandum applies to all general purpose data processing activities operated and managed by executive agencies that provide services obtainable from a private source, as defined in Circular No. A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A-76 does not authorize contracts where authority otherwise does not exist, does not override law or civil service/regulatory limits, does not apply to services provided to the public, does not apply to Government-owned contractor-operated (GOCO) activities, and should not be applied where inconsistent with treaties or international agreements. (Transmittal Memorandum ¶2; Circular ¶4)

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning and management requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must initiate program actions to implement the policy, including reviewing and revising agency instructions, emphasizing 'new starts' reviews, preparing a multiyear ADP plan for OMB, and developing program outlines with milestones and targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (a) review/revise agency ADP acquisition directives to incorporate A-76 early in planning; (b) emphasize 'new starts' to avoid unreviewed capital commitments; (c) include a multiyear plan in the Spring ADP Plan starting 1977; (d) submit a program outline with milestones/targets within 90 days. Use Management by Objectives (MBO) where appropriate. (Transmittal Memorandum ¶5; Acquisition/Planning sections)

rubrics_metrics.name: Express ADP requirements in service terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Government ADP requirements normally will be expressed in terms of the services to be performed rather than the equipment and software to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements of requirements should allow contractors maximum flexibility in type of equipment and personnel used as long as satisfactory services are provided. This supports competitive commercial solutions. (Transmittal Memorandum ¶6.a)

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation and triggers for conducting cost-comparison studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies to determine whether a commercial ADP activity can be justified on the basis of cost should be limited to situations where there is reason to assume in-house costs will be significantly less than competitive commercial prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, comparative cost analyses are not required for services estimated to cost less than $50,000 per year unless there is reason to believe commercial prices are unreasonable. Agency heads may direct studies below the threshold if warranted. Cost studies are also required before financing more than $50,000 in facilities/equipment via contracts, and in other cases where savings may be realized. (Circular ¶6)

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative cost analysis elements and inclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision based on relative costs must be supported by a comparative cost analysis that discloses the difference between Government and commercial alternatives and includes all relevant cost elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial costs should include amounts paid to suppliers, transportation, bid preparation/evaluation/management costs, costs of materials furnished by Government, charges for Government-owned equipment used by contractors, and possible premium provisions. Government costs should include: (1) personal services & benefits (full cost of retirement on normal-cost basis, Social Security where applicable, allowances, termination/separation, travel, etc.), (2) materials/supplies/utilities, (3) maintenance & repair, (4) damage/loss/insurance, (5) federal taxes (corporate income etc.), (6) depreciation with appropriate residual/salvage values (no accelerated depreciation), (7) interest computed using average yield for long-term Treasury bonds reduced over useful life on straight-line basis, and (8) indirect costs (management, budgeting, accounting, personnel, legal). Include costs of standby status or increased retirement costs where discontinuance triggers them. For ADP, account for obsolescence and uncertainty — the cost differential may need to be substantially more than 10%. (Circular ¶6.a–c; Transmittal Memorandum ¶6.c)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of valid commercial cost figure
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing a valid commercial cost figure generally requires solicitation of competitive bids and assurance that Government and commercial estimates are based on equivalent services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial firms may provide price proposals if assured of an objective cost study. Particular attention must be paid to obtaining fair market value for Government-owned equipment/facilities that would become excess if services were obtained commercially. (Circular ¶6.d; Transmittal Memorandum ¶6.c(1)–(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Required savings/differential for new starts and continuations
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'new start' or continuation for comparative cost reasons should ordinarily be justified only if Government costs are sufficiently less than commercial costs — commonly cited as at least 10% less — to outweigh risks and uncertainties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 10% is not fixed; required differential depends on circumstances (capital investment size, obsolescence risk, uncertainty of requirements). For ADP activities, the differential may be substantially more than 10% because of rapid obsolescence and uncertainty. Decisions should be reconsidered if actual bids indicate commercial prices are higher than estimated. (Circular ¶7.b.(3); Transmittal Memorandum ¶6.c)

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances justifying Government provision of commercial/industrial services (A-76 exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government commercial or industrial activity may be authorized only under specified conditions: (a) procurement from commercial source would disrupt or materially delay program; (b) necessary for combat support/mobilization or military retraining; (c) a satisfactory commercial source is not available or cannot be developed in time; (d) product/service is available from another Federal agency; (e) procurement from commercial source will result in higher cost to Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each exception requires factual review/documentation. Classified status alone is not adequate cause; urgency alone is insufficient unless commercial sources cannot meet need in time. Use assistance from GSA, SBA, BDSA in finding commercial sources. (Circular ¶5)

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory and review process for existing activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency must compile and maintain an inventory of its commercial or industrial activities having annual output costing $50,000 or more or capital investment of $25,000 or more, and conduct systematic reviews of existing activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventory should include capital investment, annual payments, and basis for continuation. 'New starts' and activities in inventory must be reviewed: initial inventory descriptive info by June 30, 1966, and reviews of activities at least once before June 30, 1968; remaining activities scheduled for at least one follow-up review each three-year period unless waived. Reviews should determine availability of commercial sources and include a report; continuation requires assistant secretary (or equivalent) approval with basis recorded. (Circular ¶7.a–c)

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration and approval of 'new starts'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'new start' must not be initiated until possibilities of obtaining the product/service from commercial sources have been explored and the activity is approved by the agency head or an assistant secretary (or equivalent) on factual justification under A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If statutory authority/funds for construction are required, A-76 actions should be completed before agency budget request is submitted. 'New starts' for comparative cost reasons should normally show substantial savings (see differential guidance). Definitions: newly established 'new start' = additional capital ≥ $25,000 or annual cost ≥ $50,000; reactivation/expansion/modernization thresholds are higher (doubled). (Circular ¶7.b; Definitions ¶3.a)

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination and transition planning
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Government commercial or industrial activity is to be terminated or reduced, action must be carefully planned to ensure transition without disruption of vital services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning should include reasonable consideration for displaced employees (phased reduction, reassignment, reduction by attrition), careful coordination of contract services including overlap periods when necessary, and inclusion of costs for standby facilities or premature retirements in cost comparisons. (Transmittal Memorandum ¶7; Circular ¶7)

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation responsibilities and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency must implement the provisions of the Circular by issuing implementing instructions, providing management support and review/followup procedures, designating a senior official with overall responsibility, and furnishing a copy of implementing instructions to the Bureau of the Budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If legislative changes are needed, agencies should prepare proposals per Circular A-19. Delegated responsibility should be assigned to a senior official reporting directly to the agency head. (Circular ¶8)

rubrics_metrics.name: Special ADP considerations: obsolescence, uncertainty, and higher differentials
rubrics_metrics.description: ADP operations have characteristics — rapid obsolescence and uncertainty of requirements — that should be reflected in cost-comparison differentials and in the assessment of comparative advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cost differential favoring commercial sources should reflect early obsolescence and uncertainty; for ADP this differential can be substantially more than the standard 10% assumed for 'new starts.' The draft memorandum emphasizes avoiding capital commitments on new ADP facilities until A-76 review. (Transmittal Memorandum ¶6.c)
